meta.title: The Common Coverdale Psalter

version.name: Psalter of the 1928 American Book of Common Prayer
The Common Coverdale (this project)
version.basis: bcp1928, with pronouns, verb forms, archaisms, and select renderings corrected toward the Hebrew

meta.notation: Each verse divides into halves at the chant asterisk. pos="a" is the first half (before the asterisk), pos="b" the second. Render as "a * b" for pointed text. Words standing for the tetragrammaton are wrapped in the dn element, with the read-aloud form ("Lord") as content; renderers apply the traditional LORD / small-caps convention.

half.text: Hear me when I call, O God of my righteousness:
Hear me when I call, O God of my righteousness;
thou hast set me at liberty when I was in trouble; have mercy upon me, and hearken unto my prayer.
you have set me at liberty when I was in trouble; have mercy upon me, and listen to my prayer.
O ye sons of men, how long will ye blaspheme mine honour,
O you children of earth, how long will you dishonor my glory,
and have such pleasure in vanity, and seek after falsehood?
and take such pleasure in vanity, and seek after falsehood?

verse.note: Coverdale's "blaspheme mine honour" (via the Latin) overstates the Hebrew, which speaks of turning the psalmist's glory to shame; hence "dishonor my glory." "Children of earth" renders the generic address bene ish.

half.text: Know this also, that the Lord hath chosen to himself the man that is godly;
Know this also, that the Lord has chosen for himself the one who is godly;
when I call upon the Lord, he will hear me.
when I call upon the Lord, he will hear me.
Stand in awe, and sin not;
Stand in awe, and do not sin;
commune with your own heart, and in your chamber, and be still.
commune with your own heart upon your bed, and be still.

verse.note: Hebrew mishkav, "bed": Coverdale's "chamber" generalizes the image. "Stand in awe" retained over the more literal "Tremble" for continuity with the Compline tradition.

half.text: Offer the sacrifice of righteousness,
Offer the sacrifice of righteousness,
and put your trust in the Lord.
and put your trust in the Lord.
There be many that say,
There are many who say,
Who will show us any good?
"Who will show us any good?"
Lord, lift thou up
Lord, lift up
the light of thy countenance upon us.
the light of your countenance upon us.
Thou hast put gladness in my heart,
You have put gladness in my heart,
since the time that their corn and wine and oil increased.
more than when their grain and wine and oil increased.

verse.note: The Hebrew is comparative: gladness greater than the harvest-rich enjoy. Coverdale's "since the time that" misreads this. "Corn" updated to "grain" (American ambiguity). "And oil" is a Vulgate inheritance absent from the Hebrew, retained as characteristic of the Coverdale tradition.

half.text: I will lay me down in peace, and take my rest;
I will lie down in peace, and take my rest;
for it is thou, Lord, only, that makest me dwell in safety.
for it is you, Lord, only, who make me dwell in safety.

verse.note: Familiar from Compline; cadence preserved for existing musical settings.

half.text: The Lord is my shepherd;
The Lord is my shepherd;
therefore can I lack nothing.
therefore I can lack nothing.
He shall feed me in a green pasture,
He shall feed me in a green pasture,
and lead me forth beside the waters of comfort.
and lead me forth beside the waters of comfort.

verse.note: "Waters of comfort" is a distinctive Coverdale phrase, retained as beloved and clear.

half.text: He shall convert my soul,
He shall restore my soul,
and bring me forth in the paths of righteousness for his Name's sake.
and bring me forth in the paths of righteousness for his Name's sake.

verse.note: "Convert" in its older sense meant "turn back, restore"; the modern religious sense misleads.

half.text: Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil;
Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil;
for thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff comfort me.
for you are with me; your rod and your staff comfort me.
Thou shalt prepare a table before me in the presence of them that trouble me;
You shall prepare a table before me in the presence of those who trouble me;
thou hast anointed my head with oil, and my cup shall be full.
you have anointed my head with oil, and my cup shall be full.
But thy loving-kindness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life;
But your loving-kindness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life;
and I will dwell in the house of the Lord for ever.
and I will dwell in the house of the Lord for ever.
In thee, O Lord, have I put my trust:
In you, O Lord, have I put my trust;
let me never be put to confusion; deliver me in thy righteousness.
let me never be put to confusion; deliver me in your righteousness.

verse.note: Verses 1-6 only: the Compline portion (In manus tuas). The remainder of the psalm awaits the full cycle.

half.text: Bow down thine ear to me;
Bow down your ear to me;
make haste to deliver me.
make haste to deliver me.
And be thou my strong rock, and house of defence,
And be my strong rock and house of defense,
that thou mayest save me.
that you may save me.
For thou art my strong rock, and my castle:
For you are my strong rock and my castle;
be thou also my guide, and lead me for thy Name's sake.
be also my guide, and lead me for your Name's sake.
Draw me out of the net that they have laid privily for me;
Draw me out of the net that they have secretly laid for me;
for thou art my strength.
for you are my strength.
Into thy hands I commend my spirit;
Into your hands I commend my spirit;
for thou hast redeemed me, O Lord, thou God of truth.
for you have redeemed me, O Lord, O God of truth.

verse.note: The nightly versicle of Compline and the words of Christ from the cross (Luke 23:46); cadence preserved unaltered apart from pronouns.

half.text: Have mercy upon me, O God, after thy great goodness;
Have mercy upon me, O God, after your great goodness;
according to the multitude of thy mercies do away mine offences.
according to the multitude of your mercies do away my offenses.
Wash me throughly from my wickedness,
Wash me thoroughly from my wickedness,
and cleanse me from my sin.
and cleanse me from my sin.
For I acknowledge my faults,
For I acknowledge my faults,
and my sin is ever before me.
and my sin is ever before me.
Against thee only have I sinned, and done this evil in thy sight;
Against you only have I sinned, and done this evil in your sight,
that thou mightest be justified in thy saying, and clear when thou art judged.
that you might be justified in your sentence, and blameless when you judge.

verse.note: "Clear when thou art judged" follows the Greek and Latin passive; the Hebrew reads "blameless when you judge," restored here.

half.text: Behold, I was shapen in wickedness,
Behold, I was formed in wickedness,
and in sin hath my mother conceived me.
and in sin my mother conceived me.
But lo, thou requirest truth in the inward parts,
But lo, you require truth in the inward parts,
and shalt make me to understand wisdom secretly.
and shall make me understand wisdom secretly.
Thou shalt purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean;
You shall purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean;
thou shalt wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.
you shall wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.
Thou shalt make me hear of joy and gladness,
You shall make me hear of joy and gladness,
that the bones which thou hast broken may rejoice.
that the bones which you have broken may rejoice.
Turn thy face from my sins,
Turn your face from my sins,
and put out all my misdeeds.
and blot out all my misdeeds.
Make me a clean heart, O God,
Make me a clean heart, O God,
and renew a right spirit within me.
and renew a right spirit within me.
Cast me not away from thy presence,
Cast me not away from your presence,
and take not thy holy Spirit from me.
and take not your holy Spirit from me.
O give me the comfort of thy help again,
O give me the comfort of your help again,
and stablish me with thy free Spirit.
and establish me with your free Spirit.
Then shall I teach thy ways unto the wicked,
Then shall I teach your ways to the wicked,
and sinners shall be converted unto thee.
and sinners shall turn back to you.
Deliver me from blood-guiltiness, O God, thou that art the God of my health;
Deliver me from bloodguilt, O God, you who are the God of my salvation;
and my tongue shall sing of thy righteousness.
and my tongue shall sing of your righteousness.

verse.note: "Health" in Coverdale regularly means "salvation" (Old English haelu); modernized accordingly here and wherever the sense is salvific rather than medical.

half.text: Thou shalt open my lips, O Lord,
You shall open my lips, O Lord,
and my mouth shall show thy praise.
and my mouth shall show forth your praise.

verse.note: The opening versicle of the daily office ("O Lord, open thou our lips") derives from this verse.

half.text: For thou desirest no sacrifice, else would I give it thee;
For you desire no sacrifice, or else I would give it;
but thou delightest not in burnt-offerings.
but you take no delight in burnt-offerings.
The sacrifice of God is a troubled spirit:
The sacrifice of God is a troubled spirit;
a broken and contrite heart, O God, shalt thou not despise.
a broken and contrite heart, O God, you shall not despise.
O God, thou art my God;
O God, you are my God;
early will I seek thee.
early will I seek you.
My soul thirsteth for thee, my flesh also longeth after thee,
My soul thirsts for you, my flesh also longs after you,
in a barren and dry land where no water is.
in a barren and dry land where no water is.
Thus have I looked for thee in holiness,
Thus have I looked for you in the sanctuary,
that I might behold thy power and glory.
that I might behold your power and glory.

verse.note: Hebrew qodesh here denotes the sanctuary, the holy place, rather than the abstract quality.

half.text: For thy loving-kindness is better than the life itself:
For your loving-kindness is better than life itself;
my lips shall praise thee.
my lips shall praise you.
As long as I live will I magnify thee on this manner,
As long as I live will I magnify you in this manner,
and lift up my hands in thy Name.
and lift up my hands in your Name.
My soul shall be satisfied, even as it were with marrow and fatness,
My soul shall be satisfied, even as it were with marrow and fatness,
when my mouth praiseth thee with joyful lips.
when my mouth praises you with joyful lips.
Have I not remembered thee in my bed,
Have I not remembered you upon my bed,
and thought upon thee when I was waking?
and thought upon you in the watches of the night?

verse.note: The Hebrew speaks of meditating in the night watches; Coverdale's "when I was waking" obscures the image.

half.text: Because thou hast been my helper;
Because you have been my helper,
therefore under the shadow of thy wings will I rejoice.
therefore under the shadow of your wings will I rejoice.
My soul hangeth upon thee;
My soul clings to you;
thy right hand hath upholden me.
your right hand has upheld me.
These also that seek the hurt of my soul,
Those also who seek the hurt of my soul,
they shall go under the earth.
they shall go down under the earth.
Let them fall upon the edge of the sword,
Let them fall upon the edge of the sword,
that they may be a portion for foxes.
that they may be a portion for jackals.

verse.note: Hebrew shu'alim: jackals, the carrion scavengers of the wilderness, not the English fox.

half.text: But the King shall rejoice in God; all they also that swear by him shall be commended;
But the King shall rejoice in God; all those also who swear by him shall be commended;
for the mouth of them that speak lies shall be stopped.
for the mouth of those who speak lies shall be stopped.
God be merciful unto us, and bless us,
God be merciful to us, and bless us,
and show us the light of his countenance, and be merciful unto us;
and show us the light of his countenance, and be merciful to us;
That thy way may be known upon earth,
That your way may be known upon earth,
thy saving health among all nations.
your saving power among all nations.

verse.note: "Saving health": Coverdale's term for salvation; see the note at Psalm 51:14.

half.text: Let the peoples praise thee, O God;
Let the peoples praise you, O God;
yea, let all the peoples praise thee.
yea, let all the peoples praise you.
O let the nations rejoice and be glad;
O let the nations rejoice and be glad;
for thou shalt judge the folk righteously, and govern the nations upon earth.
for you shall judge the peoples righteously, and govern the nations upon earth.
Let the peoples praise thee, O God;
Let the peoples praise you, O God;
yea, let all the peoples praise thee.
yea, let all the peoples praise you.
Then shall the earth bring forth her increase;
Then shall the earth bring forth her increase;
and God, even our own God, shall give us his blessing.
and God, even our own God, shall give us his blessing.
God shall bless us;
God shall bless us;
and all the ends of the world shall fear him.
and all the ends of the world shall fear him.
Whoso dwelleth under the defence of the Most High,
Whoever dwells under the defense of the Most High
shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.
shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.
I will say unto the Lord, Thou art my hope, and my stronghold;
I will say to the Lord, "You are my hope and my stronghold;
my God, in him will I trust.
my God, in whom I trust."
For he shall deliver thee from the snare of the hunter,
For he shall deliver you from the snare of the hunter
and from the noisome pestilence.
and from the deadly pestilence.

verse.note: "Noisome" now suggests noise or mere unpleasantness; its older sense was "harmful, deadly."

half.text: He shall defend thee under his wings, and thou shalt be safe under his feathers;
He shall defend you under his wings, and you shall be safe under his feathers;
his faithfulness and truth shall be thy shield and buckler.
his faithfulness and truth shall be your shield and buckler.
Thou shalt not be afraid for any terror by night,
You shall not be afraid of any terror by night,
nor for the arrow that flieth by day;
nor of the arrow that flies by day;
For the pestilence that walketh in darkness,
Of the pestilence that walks in darkness,
nor for the sickness that destroyeth in the noon-day.
nor of the sickness that destroys at noonday.
A thousand shall fall beside thee, and ten thousand at thy right hand;
A thousand shall fall beside you, and ten thousand at your right hand,
but it shall not come nigh thee.
but it shall not come near you.
Yea, with thine eyes shalt thou behold,
Yea, with your eyes you shall behold,
and see the reward of the ungodly.
and see the reward of the ungodly.
For thou, Lord, art my hope;
For you have made the Lord your hope,
thou hast set thine house of defence very high.
and the Most High your house of defense.

verse.note: Coverdale's rendering garbles the Hebrew, which reads: because you have made the LORD your refuge, the Most High your dwelling. The modern text restores the sense.

half.text: There shall no evil happen unto thee,
There shall no evil happen to you,
neither shall any plague come nigh thy dwelling.
neither shall any plague come near your dwelling.
For he shall give his angels charge over thee,
For he shall give his angels charge over you,
to keep thee in all thy ways.
to keep you in all your ways.
They shall bear thee in their hands,
They shall bear you in their hands,
that thou hurt not thy foot against a stone.
lest you hurt your foot against a stone.
Thou shalt go upon the lion and adder:
You shall tread upon the lion and adder;
the young lion and the dragon shalt thou tread under thy feet.
the young lion and the serpent you shall trample underfoot.

verse.note: "Dragon" renders Hebrew tannin, a serpent or sea-creature; "serpent" avoids the modern mythological sense.

half.text: Because he hath set his love upon me, therefore will I deliver him;
"Because he has set his love upon me, therefore will I deliver him;
I will set him up, because he hath known my Name.
I will lift him up, because he has known my Name.
He shall call upon me, and I will hear him;
He shall call upon me, and I will hear him;
yea, I am with him in trouble; I will deliver him, and bring him to honour.
yea, I am with him in trouble; I will deliver him and bring him to honor.
With long life will I satisfy him,
With long life will I satisfy him,
and show him my salvation.
and show him my salvation."
It is a good thing to give thanks unto the Lord,
It is a good thing to give thanks to the Lord,
and to sing praises unto thy Name, O Most Highest;
and to sing praises to your Name, O Most High;
To tell of thy loving-kindness early in the morning,
To tell of your loving-kindness early in the morning,
and of thy truth in the night season;
and of your truth in the night season;
Upon an instrument of ten strings, and upon the lute;
Upon an instrument of ten strings, and upon the lute;
upon a loud instrument, and upon the harp.
upon a loud instrument, and upon the harp.
For thou, Lord, hast made me glad through thy works;
For you, Lord, have made me glad through your works;
and I will rejoice in giving praise for the operations of thy hands.
and I will rejoice in giving praise for the works of your hands.
O Lord, how glorious are thy works!
O Lord, how glorious are your works!
thy thoughts are very deep.
Your thoughts are very deep.
An unwise man doth not well consider this,
An unwise person does not well consider this,
and a fool doth not understand it.
and a fool does not understand it.
When the ungodly are green as the grass, and when all the workers of wickedness do flourish,
When the ungodly are green as the grass, and when all the workers of wickedness flourish,
then shall they be destroyed for ever; but thou, Lord, art the Most Highest for evermore.
then shall they be destroyed for ever; but you, Lord, are the Most High for evermore.
For lo, thine enemies, O Lord, lo, thine enemies shall perish;
For lo, your enemies, O Lord, lo, your enemies shall perish;
and all the workers of wickedness shall be destroyed.
and all the workers of wickedness shall be destroyed.
But mine horn shall be exalted like the horn of an unicorn;
But my horn shall be exalted like the horn of a wild ox;
for I am anointed with fresh oil.
for I am anointed with fresh oil.

verse.note: Hebrew re'em, the wild ox; "unicorn" entered the tradition through the Greek monokeros and the Latin unicornis.

half.text: Mine eye also shall see his lust of mine enemies,
My eye also shall see the downfall of my enemies,
and mine ear shall hear his desire of the wicked that arise up against me.
and my ear shall hear the ruin of the wicked who rise up against me.

verse.note: Coverdale's "his lust of mine enemies" is Tudor idiom for "my desire upon my enemies," i.e. seeing their defeat; the modern text renders the sense.

half.text: The righteous shall flourish like a palm-tree,
The righteous shall flourish like a palm tree,
and shall spread abroad like a cedar in Lebanon.
and shall spread abroad like a cedar of Lebanon.

verse.note: "Lebanon" is itself a 1928 revision of the older books' "Libanus," on the pattern documented at Psalm 104.

half.text: Such as are planted in the house of the Lord
Those who are planted in the house of the Lord
shall flourish in the courts of the house of our God.
shall flourish in the courts of the house of our God.
They also shall bring forth more fruit in their age,
They also shall bring forth more fruit in their age,
and shall be fat and well-liking.
and shall be green and flourishing.

verse.note: "Fat and well-liking" meant thriving and in good condition; the modern phrase keeps the image of the evergreen tree.

half.text: That they may show how true the Lord my strength is,
That they may show how true the Lord my strength is,
and that there is no unrighteousness in him.
and that there is no unrighteousness in him.
O come, let us sing unto the Lord;
O come, let us sing to the Lord;
let us heartily rejoice in the strength of our salvation.
let us heartily rejoice in the strength of our salvation.
Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving,
Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving,
and show ourselves glad in him with psalms.
and show ourselves glad in him with psalms.
For the Lord is a great God,
For the Lord is a great God,
and a great King above all gods.
and a great King above all gods.
In his hand are all the corners of the earth,
In his hand are all the corners of the earth,
and the strength of the hills is his also.
and the strength of the hills is his also.
The sea is his, and he made it;
The sea is his, and he made it;
and his hands prepared the dry land.
and his hands prepared the dry land.
O come, let us worship and fall down,
O come, let us worship and bow down,
and kneel before the Lord our Maker.
and kneel before the Lord our Maker.

verse.note: "Fall down" now reads as accident; "bow down" restores the intended act of homage.

half.text: For he is the Lord our God,
For he is the Lord our God,
and we are the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand.
and we are the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand.
To-day if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts,
Today if you will hear his voice, harden not your hearts,
as in the provocation, and as in the day of temptation in the wilderness;
as at the rebellion, and as in the day of testing in the wilderness;

verse.note: "Provocation" and "temptation" translate the place-names Meribah and Massah; "rebellion" and "testing" render their meanings for modern ears.

half.text: When your fathers tempted me,
When your forebears put me to the test,
proved me, and saw my works.
they tried me, though they had seen my works.
Forty years long was I grieved with this generation, and said,
Forty years long I grieved over that generation, and said,
It is a people that do err in their hearts, for they have not known my ways;
It is a people that go astray in their hearts, for they have not known my ways;
Unto whom I sware in my wrath,
To whom I swore in my wrath,
that they should not enter into my rest.
that they should never enter my rest.
O sing unto the Lord a new song;
O sing to the Lord a new song,
for he hath done marvellous things.
for he has done marvelous things.
With his own right hand, and with his holy arm,
With his own right hand and with his holy arm
hath he gotten himself the victory.
he has won himself the victory.
The Lord declared his salvation;
The Lord declared his salvation;
his righteousness hath he openly showed in the sight of the heathen.
his righteousness he has openly shown in the sight of the nations.

verse.note: The 1928 book retains "heathen" here, unlike the passages it revised to "nations"; the modern text completes the change.

half.text: He hath remembered his mercy and truth toward the house of Israel;
He has remembered his mercy and truth toward the house of Israel,
and all the ends of the world have seen the salvation of our God.
and all the ends of the world have seen the salvation of our God.
Show yourselves joyful unto the Lord, all ye lands;
Show yourselves joyful to the Lord, all you lands;
sing, rejoice, and give thanks.
sing, rejoice, and give thanks.
Praise the Lord upon the harp;
Praise the Lord upon the harp;
sing to the harp with a psalm of thanksgiving.
sing to the harp with a psalm of thanksgiving.
With trumpets also and shawms,
With trumpets also and the sound of the horn,
O show yourselves joyful before the Lord the King.
O show yourselves joyful before the Lord the King.

verse.note: The shawm, a Renaissance double-reed instrument, translated the Hebrew shofar, the ram's horn; the modern text returns to the horn.

half.text: Let the sea make a noise, and all that therein is;
Let the sea make a noise, and all that is in it,
the round world, and they that dwell therein.
the round world, and those who dwell therein.
Let the floods clap their hands, and let the hills be joyful together before the Lord;
Let the floods clap their hands, and let the hills be joyful together before the Lord,
for he is come to judge the earth.
for he has come to judge the earth.
With righteousness shall he judge the world,
With righteousness shall he judge the world,
and the peoples with equity.
and the peoples with equity.
O be joyful in the Lord, all ye lands:
O be joyful in the Lord, all you lands;
serve the Lord with gladness, and come before his presence with a song.
serve the Lord with gladness, and come before his presence with a song.
Be ye sure that the Lord he is God; it is he that hath made us, and not we ourselves;
Be sure that the Lord, he is God; it is he who has made us, and we are his;
we are his people, and the sheep of his pasture.
we are his people, and the sheep of his pasture.

verse.note: "Not we ourselves" follows the written Hebrew text (lo, "not"); the read tradition (lo, "to him") gives "and we are his," adopted by most modern versions and here.

half.text: O go your way into his gates with thanksgiving, and into his courts with praise;
O go your way into his gates with thanksgiving, and into his courts with praise;
be thankful unto him, and speak good of his Name.
be thankful to him, and speak good of his Name.
For the Lord is gracious, his mercy is everlasting;
For the Lord is gracious, his mercy is everlasting;
and his truth endureth from generation to generation.
and his truth endures from generation to generation.
O praise the Lord, all ye nations;
O praise the Lord, all you nations;
praise him, all ye peoples.
praise him, all you peoples.

verse.note: "Nations" and "peoples" are themselves 1928 revisions: earlier books read "heathen" and "people."

half.text: For his merciful kindness is ever more and more toward us;
For his merciful kindness is ever more and more toward us;
and the truth of the Lord endureth for ever. Praise the Lord.
and the truth of the Lord endures for ever. Praise the Lord.
I will lift up mine eyes unto the hills;
I will lift up my eyes to the hills;
from whence cometh my help?
from where is my help to come?

verse.note: Question mark introduced in 1928; earlier American and English books print a period, reading the line as a statement. The interrogative follows the Hebrew.

half.text: My help cometh even from the Lord,
My help comes even from the Lord,
who hath made heaven and earth.
who has made heaven and earth.
He will not suffer thy foot to be moved;
He will not let your foot be moved;
and he that keepeth thee will not sleep.
and he who keeps you will not sleep.
Behold, he that keepeth Israel
Behold, he who keeps Israel
shall neither slumber nor sleep.
shall neither slumber nor sleep.
The Lord himself is thy keeper;
The Lord himself is your keeper;
the Lord is thy defence upon thy right hand;
the Lord is your defense upon your right hand;
So that the sun shall not burn thee by day,
So that the sun shall not strike you by day,
neither the moon by night.
neither the moon by night.

verse.note: Hebrew nakah, "smite/strike": "strike" covers both sunstroke and the traditional fear of moonstroke, where "burn" fits only the sun.

half.text: The Lord shall preserve thee from all evil;
The Lord shall preserve you from all evil;
yea, it is even he that shall keep thy soul.
yea, it is even he who shall keep your soul.
The Lord shall preserve thy going out, and thy coming in,
The Lord shall preserve your going out and your coming in,
from this time forth for evermore.
from this time forth for evermore.
Out of the deep have I called unto thee, O Lord;
Out of the deep have I called to you, O Lord;
Lord, hear my voice.
Lord, hear my voice.
O let thine ears consider well
O let your ears consider well
the voice of my complaint.
the voice of my supplication.

verse.note: "Complaint" in its older sense meant a plea or lament, not a grievance; "supplication" restores the sense.

half.text: If thou, Lord, wilt be extreme to mark what is done amiss,
If you, Lord, should be extreme to mark what is done amiss,
O Lord, who may abide it?
O Lord, who could abide it?
For there is mercy with thee;
For there is mercy with you;
therefore shalt thou be feared.
therefore you shall be feared.
I look for the Lord; my soul doth wait for him;
I look for the Lord; my soul waits for him;
in his word is my trust.
in his word is my trust.
My soul fleeth unto the Lord before the morning watch;
My soul waits for the Lord more than watchmen for the morning;
I say, before the morning watch.
more, I say, than watchmen for the morning.

verse.note: Coverdale's "fleeth unto the Lord before the morning watch" loses the Hebrew comparison: the soul waits for the LORD more eagerly than sentries wait for dawn. The 1928 revision itself adjusted this verse's punctuation from earlier books.

half.text: Lord, I call upon thee; haste thee unto me,

verse.note: The foundational verse of evening prayer across the traditions, sung at Orthodox vespers and in modern Western evening rites; wording untouched apart from the pronoun.

verse.note: The 1928 revision itself recast this verse and the next from the older books' wording.

half.text: Let the righteous rather smite me friendly, and reprove me;

verse.note: "Smite me friendly" — a kindly rebuke — is charming but now opaque; the oil is the anointing oil of hospitality.
